LocaliQ’s 2026 Google Ads Benchmarks study (analyzing 13,474 U.S. search campaigns across 23 industries) reveals where ad spend is actually going: → Attorneys & Legal Services remain the single highest-priced category at $9.87 per click. → Home & Home Improvement average CPC jumped to $8.33, up from $7.85 the year prior. → Broad across-the-board CPC inflation means bidding blind is more dangerous than ever. When clicks push into the $8–$10+ territory, paid search stops being a simple faucet you turn on and off. A wasted click isn’t pocket change anymore; it’s a direct hit to your operating margin. If your ad spend is rising while conversions stay flat, the problem usually isn't the bid—it's a broken pipeline between the click and your operations. At these prices, you can’t afford leaky landing pages, weak follow-up, or unoptimized keyword waste. Family law · South Florida

# Same cost per lead in three counties. _The leads weren't worth the same._

Segarra & Associates, P.A. ran $2,500 a month across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach, producing about 50 leads a month at roughly $50 each. The acquisition cost barely moved between counties. What the resulting cases were worth moved considerably, and in divorce work, that's the number that matters.

Client Segarra & Associates, P.A.

Practice Divorce & child custody

Market Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach

Engagement 1 year · $2,500/mo

  Case Study: About the Client   

segarralawfirm.com

![Segarra and Associates website](https://discovermybusiness.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Segarra-Associates-image1.webp)

About the client

## A South Florida firm advertising across three different markets.

**Segarra & Associates, P.A.** handles divorce and child custody matters across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach, three adjacent counties that are convenient to describe as South Florida and behave very differently as advertising markets.

We were brought in to run Google Ads across all three counties, structured so each could be read on its own rather than blended into one regional average.

  Case Study: The Idea   

The idea that shaped the account

## Divorce work scales with assets. Cost per lead doesn't.

Two divorce clients can have the same charge sheet, so to speak, and entirely different files. One has a rented apartment and a shared car. The other has a house, a business, retirement accounts, and a spousal support dispute. The second matter involves far more work, and the advertising that produced both leads cost the same.

What the ad account sees

### Fifty leads at fifty dollars.

A clean, consistent number that looks identical across every county in the campaign. It tells you the advertising is working and tells you nothing at all about which of those leads turned into substantial work.

*   Measured **Cost per lead**
*   Varies by county **Barely**
*   Case complexity **Invisible**
*   Decision it supports **Almost none**

What the firm sees

### Fifty leads, unevenly valuable.

The firm reported that matters originating in Palm Beach tended to involve clients with more substantial assets, and correspondingly more substantial cases. Same acquisition cost, materially different work, a difference only visible on their side of the funnel.

*   Measured **Case value**
*   Varies by county **Considerably**
*   Case complexity **Visible**
*   Decision it supports **Where to spend**

  Case Study: Starting Position   

Starting position

## Three counties, treated as one market.

Segarra & Associates, P.A. handles divorce and child custody matters across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach, three adjacent counties that are convenient to describe as South Florida and behave very differently as advertising markets.

Four things shaped the account.

*   #### A modest budget across a large population
    
    $2,500 a month covering three of Florida's most populous counties. Spread evenly, that's a thin presence everywhere; concentrated, it's a real presence somewhere.
    
*   #### Family law is a long decision
    
    People research divorce for months before acting. Nothing here is urgent, which changes the messaging and means the same person may see the firm repeatedly before making contact.
    
*   #### Divorce and custody aren't the same enquiry
    
    Someone deciding whether to file and someone in a custody dispute are at different stages with different fears, even when they eventually become the same client.
    
*   #### Case value lives outside the ad account
    
    Nothing in Google Ads knows what a matter will bill. Without the firm telling us which enquiries became substantial cases, county level budget decisions would have been guesses.
    

  Case Study: The Build   

The build

## Four decisions on $2,500 a month.

Three counties is a lot of ground for this budget.

01

#### Separate the counties from the start

Each county given its own campaign rather than one South Florida target. It costs nothing extra to structure this way and it's the only way to see whether the three markets behave differently, which, as it turned out, they did.

Three readable markets instead of one blended figure.

02

#### Split divorce from custody

The two practice areas given their own campaigns and messaging, so someone considering filing and someone already in a custody dispute each saw something written for where they actually were.

Messaging matched to the stage of the decision.

03

#### Accept both calls and forms, properly

Call tracking alongside form capture, with both given prominence. Sixty percent of leads came by phone and forty percent by form, a far more even split than our criminal defence accounts, because family law decisions are made over weeks rather than in a night.

Both routes measured, neither assumed.

04

#### Ask the firm which leads became real cases

Lead volume and cost per lead came from the account. Which enquiries turned into substantial matters came from the firm, and only the combination of the two says anything useful about where the budget should sit.

A county level finding the ad data alone couldn't produce.

  Case Study: The Finding   

The finding

## Palm Beach produced better work at the same price.

*   Monthly budget **$2,500**
*   Phone calls **~30**
*   Contact forms **~20**
*   Total leads **~50**
*   Cost per lead **~$50**

Those figures held reasonably steady across the three counties. What didn't hold steady was what happened after the enquiry, the firm found that matters originating in Palm Beach tended to involve clients with more substantial assets, and therefore more substantial cases.

In divorce work the file grows with what there is to divide. Property, a business, retirement accounts, spousal support, **each of those adds work that a straightforward separation simply doesn't involve.** A lead is a lead. A case isn't a case.

Which makes geography one of the few usable proxies a family law firm has. You cannot target by household assets, and you shouldn't try. But you can observe which areas produce the matters your practice is built to handle, and weight the budget toward them.

### Why this only works if the firm tells you
